name: Hollow Hold
description: The hollow hold is a foundational gymnastics isometric that trains the entire anterior chain in a compressed, coordinated position. The athlete lies supine, pressing the lower back into the floor, tucking the pelvis posteriorly, and raising the arms, shoulders, and legs off the floor while maintaining a curved, rigid body shape. It develops the rectus abdominis and transverse abdominis under sustained tension and serves as a prerequisite for many advanced calisthenics skills.

execution.starting_position: Lie flat on your back on the floor with your arms extended overhead and legs straight. Your entire back should be in contact with the floor.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Find a flat, firm surface with enough length to extend your body fully.
steps: Step 1: Lie on your back with arms extended overhead and legs straight.
Step 2: Exhale fully and press your lower back firmly into the floor by posteriorly tilting the pelvis.
Step 3: Raise your arms, shoulders, and head off the floor while simultaneously lifting your legs to approximately 30–45 degrees.
Step 4: Point your toes, squeeze your thighs together, and hold the curved position for the prescribed duration.
Step 5: Breathe shallowly through the nose to maintain tension. Lower with control when done.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale deeply to initiate the brace, then breathe shallowly through the nose during the hold. Avoid taking large breaths that cause the lower back to lift.
common_mistakes: Allowing the lower back to arch away from the floor
Raising the legs too high, which reduces core challenge
Relaxing the shoulder and neck position midway through the hold
Holding the breath instead of breathing shallowly
safety_considerations: If the lower back cannot stay flat on the floor, raise the legs higher or bend the knees to reduce the lever arm.
Avoid if experiencing acute lower back pain.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: The body should form a shallow concave curve from fingertips to toes. The lower back must remain in contact with the floor throughout.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Hold for 20–60 seconds. Progress duration before adding any weight or hollow body variations.
coaching_cues: Press your belly button to the floor
Make your body look like a banana
Think long and tight — squeeze everything
